hero.title: Am I ready for a new relationship? The test to find out
hero.description: You've been single for a few months, or a few years, and someone is starting to catch your eye. Is this the right moment? This test looks at the room your ex still takes up, what you're looking for in someone and the life you're living today.
hero.subtitle: Twenty questions, four minutes, a result on five levels

section1.title: How do you know if you're ready to be in a couple again?
section1.intro: The question almost always comes up at the same moment: when someone starts to matter, or when a friend tells you "it's about time...". And the answer isn't obvious, because you want it to be yes.
section1.p1: Being ready for a new relationship doesn't mean you've finished thinking about your ex. Nobody quite finishes. It's more that the memory has changed place: it no longer decides your evenings, it no longer slips into every new encounter to compare. You can talk about it without your voice changing.
section1.p2: It's also a question of what you want. There's a big difference between wanting someone and wanting this particular person. The first wish comes from lack. The bed is too big, the Sundays are too long, and everyone around you is in a couple. The second comes from curiosity. When it's lack that pushes, you take the first kind person who comes along. That has a name, by the way: the rebound relationship.
section1.p3: And then there's your own life, the one you're living right now. People often forget it, when it counts as much as the rest. Someone with a full life can welcome a relationship. Someone whose life is empty will ask the relationship to fill it, and that's too heavy for anyone.

section2.title: The four things the test looks at closely
section2.sub1Title: The room your ex still takes up
section2.sub1P1: This is what weighs most in the calculation. It's not that thinking about your ex is forbidden. It's that it damages the next relationship more than anything else. If you still compare, if you keep their messages to reread them, if you don't know what you'd do if they came back, the place isn't free. If you're still wondering what your ex thinks of you, that's often a sign the chapter isn't quite closed.
section2.sub2Title: What you're looking for, deep down
section2.sub2P1: Sharing, or filling? The test asks the question in several ways, because people rarely answer truthfully the first time. Someone who mostly wants to stop being alone in the evenings isn't in the same place as someone who feels like getting to know a person. Someone who wants to prove something to their ex even less so. Both wishes are human, but they don't lead to the same relationship.
section2.sub3P1: The test asks what you do with a Friday evening on your own, whether you have projects that are moving forward, and what the people close to you say about you right now. It seems beside the point. In fact, it's the best sign that you can let someone into your life without asking everything of them.
section2.sub4P1: Two or three questions look at what you do when you like someone: you dive in, you wait, or you cut it off before it starts. And what you do with time for yourself once you're in a couple. That's your way of attaching, and it says a lot about how the next relationship will begin.

section3.title: How the test works out your result
section3.p1: Twenty questions, four answers each time. Every answer earns points, and the questions don't all carry the same weight. Those about your ex and about what you're looking for are worth up to six points. Those about your evenings or your projects are worth three. That's deliberate. You can perfectly well spend a Friday alone without any problem and not be ready at all. On the other hand, wanting to get back in touch with your ex says just about everything.
section3.p2: The total comes to 86 points. The result reads on five levels, from "not now" to "ready, for good", each time with what your answers say and one thing to do. Nobody sees your answers, and you can take the test again in three months. It's even a good idea, the number moves!
section3.p3: This test is about timing. It doesn't say why your dates don't lead anywhere, or whether life as a couple is right for you. Those are two other questions. If what worries you is more what gets in the way when you meet people, there's a test for that. And if you're hesitating for good between a life as a couple and a life on your own, there's another one.

seo.faq1Q: How long should you wait after a break-up before a new relationship?
seo.faq1A: There's no waiting time that works for everyone. You hear "half the length of the relationship", or "a year", but those are made-up rules. What counts is the state you're in. Can you talk about your ex without it turning you upside down? Does the wish come from curiosity, or from lack? Some people are ready in three months, others need two years.
seo.faq2Q: I still think about my ex, can I still meet someone?
seo.faq2A: Yes, as long as you know it. Thinking about your ex from time to time, everyone does it, even in a happy couple. The real problem comes when the new person becomes mainly a way of not thinking about them anymore. In that case, be honest with yourself about what you're looking for, and don't promise more than you can keep.
seo.faq3A: It's a relationship you start so it stops hurting, not for the person. It does you good for a few weeks, because it fills the hole your ex left. And then, once you feel better, you realise you don't have much to say to the other person. The one who serves as the bandage, most of the time, didn't choose to. That's why the question "why now?" weighs so much in this test.
seo.faq4Q: The test says I'm not ready. What do I do?
seo.faq4A: Nothing special, and above all don't force yourself. Pick up what you set aside during the relationship. Put away what's left of your ex. See your friends. If the sadness doesn't shift after a few months, talk to a professional, it's not an admission of weakness. And take the test again later: the result changes over time, it's a snapshot of the moment.
seo.faq5A: Yes. Your answers stay in your browser, nobody sees them, and there's nothing to create or fill in. The result appears straight away at the end of the twenty questions.
